text:
Maria: Quick sync — I'm worried our bench -> runtime gap keeps growing for new intakes. bench says p95 < 120ms but prod reports p95 ~ 240ms on same model variant. We need a small set of guardrails for the onboarding pipeline so benches are predictive, not optimistic.

Ajay: Could be differences in batching profiles and KV cache hit rates. Bench uses synthetic steady traffic; real traffic is spiky.

Henry: Also quantized binaries behave differently under continuous batching vs single-request paths. Bench harness currently forces fixed batch sizes.

Leah: I ran replayed traces yesterday; the main delta was prefix length — bench inputs are short (<=64) while customer traces had a lot of 512 prefixes.

Maria: Right. Proposed follow-up: add two things to intake checks: 1) traffic-shaped microbenching (replay sampled traces and tail queuing), 2) a compatibility delta check that flags >20% increase in p95 between bench-replay and bench-synth. Thoughts?

Sam: Sounds good. For traffic-shaped microbenching we should include a small KV-miss simulation. Many models warm KV usage differently.

Ajay: We can make the probe harness configurable: pass --trace-replay <trace_id> and --kv-miss-rate 0.1. Example command: `./bench_runner --model $BINARY --trace-replay traces/recent.tar --kv-miss-rate 0.1`

Henry: We should be careful about test runtime costs. Replay can be expensive. Maybe do a lightweight replay (sample 5% of golden traces) and a full replay only for big diffs.

Leah: Agree. Two-stage approach: quick replay smoke (5%/10K tokens) and, if p95 delta > threshold, run expanded replay (50% sample or 100k tokens).

Maria: Good. Also need to codify interface between "admit validator" and "bench harness": validator should accept a small matrix of expected bench deltas and runtime heatmap. If validator sees an out-of-band delta it rejects the intake or requires an ops review.

Ajay: Proposal for validator payload (simple JSON):
```
{
  "bench_synth_p95": "110ms",
  "bench_replay_p95": "230ms",
  "kv_miss_rate": "0.1",
  "prefix_distribution": "[64:80%, 256:15%, 512:5%]"
}
```
Validator checks: (bench_replay_p95 / bench_synth_p95) <= 1.2 OR else flag.

Sam: The ratio idea is simple but brittle for very low base latencies. Maybe use absolute floors too (e.g., if replay_p95 - synth_p95 > 80ms flag).

Henry: Both checks: ratio and absolute delta. That covers both extremes.

Leah: We should also capture model binary config: quantization type, kernel hints, and whether the runtime used continuous batching. Those affect behavior. Validator should store them in the model record so we can trace regressions.

Maria: Agreed. Add fields: `quant_type`, `kernel_profile`, `continuous_batching=true/false`. Keep schema small.

Ajay: One more runtime mismatch we saw: bench runs on a hot GPU with warmed cuBLAS caches; cold-start cold caches in prod cause tail regressions. Maybe include a warmup-run flag. Bench should include both warm and cold path measurements.

Sam: We can schedule bench warmup: run `N` inferences to prefill caches, then measure warm path; then restart the process and measure cold path for a few requests. N could be 1000 tokens by default.

Henry: Operationally we need to prevent the validator from blocking many small model intakes. Suggest a severity scheme: 
- INFO: delta observed < threshold
- WARN: delta moderate, auto-canary in dedicated env for 24h
- FAIL: delta > big threshold, require dev signoff before admission

Leah: That plays nicely with canary automation. WARN triggers canary rollout with traffic split 5% for 24h and auto-rollback if error/latency SLOs breach.

Maria: Action items: 
- Ajay: PR with trace-replay flags + kv-miss sim for bench_runner (due Tue 03/30).
- Henry: Prototype validator JSON schema and ratio+absolute checks (due Wed 03/31).
- Leah: Work with infra to add warm/cold measurements to bench infra and cheap 5% replay sampling (due Fri 04/02).
- Sam: Draft canary policy mapping warnings -> rollout steps and thresholds (due Fri 04/02).

Sam: I'll put a stubbed RFC in the onboarding docs and link the PRs.

Ajay: Quick note: CI bot will run bench smoke on PRs; `ci-bot` can we add a label if bench smoke delta > 10%?

ci-bot: noted. I will add the label `bench-delta` to PRs where quick-replay p95 delta > 10% (configurable). @Ajay please open an issue to set the exact threshold.

Maria: Thanks. One more: we should include a short example in the intake UI showing expected deltas and common causes (prefix lengths, quantization). That helps reviewers.

Leah: I'll add the UI copy. Short bullet list + link to debug playbook.

Henry: FYI, we might need to extend model metadata to store `last_replay_trace_id` and `last_replay_stats` so we can diff over time.

Maria: Good catch. Make sure validator writes that metadata even for WARN cases.

Sam: Ok team — looks like we have a plan. I'll collate the issues and link them to the RFC stub.

Maria: Thanks — ping me on the PRs if you want a quick review. :thumbsup:
